REVIEWED EVIDENCE EXCERPT — NOT A COMPLETE MANUAL OR A NETWORK SCAN
6.3.1. What are Control
Charts?
https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section3/pmc31.htm
Publisher: NIST / SEMATECH
Sections: e-Handbook §6.3.1, Strategies for dealing with out-of-control findings; e-Handbook §6.3.1, monitoring and in-control interpretation
Rights: NIST employee non-SRD text generally not copyright-protected in US under 17 USC 105; handbook co-produced with SEMATECH, so no blanket public-domain assertion; limited attributed research quotations only.
Change notice: selected excerpts; whitespace normalized. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt and licenses/.
If a data point falls outside the control limits, we assume that the process is probably out of control
an investigation is warranted to find and eliminate the cause or causes.
Control charts are used to routinely monitor quality.
"in control" implies that all points are between the control limits and they form a random pattern.
